answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that cannot be copied: each agent earns a unique cipher-bound identity through verifiable work history, so spawning a fresh identity costs real effort. Sybils then face a terrace of escalating trust — new agents start on the lowest terrace with tiny limits, while proven ones climb only after consistent, useful behavior. A single relic of past fraud, recorded on-ledger, permanently caps that identity's privileges.
